title: Sherematta charged with assault
article: Two Kamloops RCMP officers have been charged with assault in separate incidents stemming from earlier this year.
Const. Ryan Sheremetta has been charged with assault after he allegedly punched another man, Ian Mcleod, in a street fight near a local bar on March 7.
Sheremetta, who was off duty at the time of the assault allegation, was involved in a high-profile fatal shooting in 2004 when he worked in Vanderhoof.

Last year, the Commission for Public Complaints Against the RCMP found Sheremetta was justified in the shooting death of Kevin St. Arnaud, despite various contradictions in testimony at the 2007 coroner's inquest between Sheremetta and other witnesses, including Sheremetta's partner that night, Colleen Erickson.
In addition, forensic evidence did not mesh with Sheremetta's claim that he was on his back and shot upwards at an advancing St. Arnaud.
The shooting took place in the early-morning hours of Dec. 19, 2004. St. Arnaud was a suspect in a pharmacy burglary and fled across a nearby soccer field.
When Sheremetta pursued him, St. Arnaud turned and rushed at him. Sheremetta fired three shots, which hit St. Arnaud in the hand and chest, killing him.
Sheremetta was suspended in 2008 after he was accused of giving false testimony during the coroner's inquest.
Const. Kevin Roy is also facing two counts of assault stemming from a pair of on-duty incidents in January involving allegations of excessive force during arrests.
Roy is accused of assaulting Jason Sorensen and Katherine Hyatt.

Roy, a member of the RCMP for just nine months, has been suspended from duty with pay, while Sheremetta, a seven-year veteran who transfered to Kamloops in 2005, has been re-assigned to administrative duties.
The investigations into both officer was handled internally by Kamloops RCMP.
Insp. Yves Lacasse said other members of the force are taking the news hard.
"It is tough," he said,
Lacasse called the allegations "serious," but cautioned the public to allow the officers to have their day in court.
"These folks are just like any other people out there. They have not been convicted of any crime," he said.
In the case of Roy, the allegations were made by the victims, while in Sheremetta's case, the allegation came from a fellow officer.
Lacasse applauded the decision of the officer to come forward.
"It's not an easy thing to do, but it's the right thing to do," he said.
Lacasse defended the investigation, saying the process proved the RCMP can be "fair" and "impartial."
The two Mounties will make their first court appearances on July 29.
